[Thinking]
**Explaining table caption alignment**

The user wants to left-align a table caption without using the caption package. I need to explore methods like using \captionof, but since they don’t want the caption package, options include manually adjusting \@makecaption or wrapping the caption text in \raggedright. For instance, I can use \caption{\raggedright Caption text\par}, which works nicely for tables. Alternatively, I could redefine \@makecaption, modifying code to achieve the left-aligned style they desire without the package.**Clarifying caption alignment methods**

I need to simplify the code for left-aligning captions. One way is using the local method with \caption{\raggedright ...\par}. The second option is redefining \@makecaption globally with a code snippet, which looks like this: \makeatletter\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{\vskip\abovecaptionskip\noindent\hbox to\hsize{\parbox[b]{\hsize}{\textbf{#1.} #2}}\vskip\belowcaptionskip}\makeatother. It’s important to mention moving arguments and potential warnings. I could also suggest using a short caption for tables in the table of contents.
[/Thinking]

Two simple ways — one local (per-caption) and one global (all captions) — without loading the caption package.

1) Local (per caption)
Use \raggedright (and end with \par) inside the caption. This is the easiest:

\begin{table}[ht]
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{...}
    ...
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{\raggedright Short label for LoT\par
    This is the full left-aligned caption text that will be set ragged-right.}
  \label{tab:example}
\end{table}

Notes:
- Put \par at the end of the caption text so the ragged-right setting stops there.
- If you want a shorter text in the list of tables, use the optional argument:
  \caption[Short LoT entry]{\raggedright Full left-aligned caption\par}

2) Global (all captions)
Redefine LaTeX's \@makecaption to change the default centering. Put this in your preamble:

\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent
  \begin{minipage}{\linewidth}%
    \let\footnotesize\small % keep size similar to default, adjust if desired
    \textbf{#1.}\ #2\par
  \end{minipage}%
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip
}
\makeatother

This code:
- Removes centering and places the caption text in a full-width minipage so it is left-aligned.
- Keeps the label (e.g. "Table 1.") in bold. Adjust formatting as you prefer.

Caveats
- Redefining \@makecaption is a low-level change; test with your document class and floats.
- If you still want ragged-right line breaks, wrap the caption text in \raggedright (either locally or modify the global definition).
- For multilingual documents or other packages that tweak captions, the caption package is safer; use these methods only if you must avoid that package.

If you want, tell me your document class and a minimal example and I can give a tailored snippet.
